This is comparatively strong provenance and exact-span evidence, but not proof of manual transcription or audio correctness for every example.

Unused train/dev material from the same corpus remains a possible source after exact deduplication and split-aware selection.

local_datasets.transcription_evidence: The local README documents scripted speech and human up-vote/down-vote validation of whether clips match the sentence. quality_notes: The validated split has the clearest local human audio-text review evidence among the broad local corpora.
Many prompts derive from a text corpus; evaluate read-speech versus conversational-audio fit separately.
Many unused clips and splits remain after ID/hash deduplication; prior use of some test examples does not eliminate the corpus.

recommendation: For stronger local evidence, prioritize unused AISHELL-1 records with official transcript/NER provenance and Common Voice validated clips with documented human match votes, after exact source-ID/audio-hash deduplication. Treat this as stronger provenance, not guaranteed audio truth. WenetSpeech TEST_NET and FLEURS are viable review candidates only after human listening. Hold MultiMed records with any known audio/reference mismatch pending item-level checks; AASR-Bench is not ready because its local audio files and annotation provenance are missing.
exclusions: No 181 references or review-input references were opened; only unseen/summary.json was used for aggregate source and hash metadata.
No audio clip was played or enumerated by filename. Corpus sizes/counts came from manifests, readmes, and aggregate filesystem metadata.
No external sources were consulted; named datasets absent locally may exist elsewhere or be downloadable, which this inventory does not assess.
